description: The tone and colour correction commands under Image > Adjustments and their non-destructive equivalents in the Adjustments panel. Each entry gives the menu path, the key controls and a worked example; adjustment layers are always preferred over the destructive menu command where both exist.

tools.name: New Adjustment Layer
tools.description: Creates any of the sixteen adjustment types as a separate, re-editable layer with its own mask and blend mode instead of baking the change into pixels. The adjustment affects every layer below it unless it is clipped (Alt+Ctrl+G) or placed inside a group whose mode is not Pass Through. This is the correct way to make every adjustment listed in this category.
tools.usage: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > <type>, the half-filled circle button at the bottom of the Layers panel, or the icons in Window > Adjustments.

parameters.name: Mask
parameters.description: Created automatically; paint black to exclude areas, or load a selection before creating the layer.

parameters.name: Clip to Layer
parameters.description: The left-hand button in the Properties panel confines the adjustment to the layer directly below.

parameters.name: Blend mode
parameters.description: Setting a Curves or Levels layer to Luminosity prevents saturation shifts.

tools.name: Brightness/Contrast
tools.description: The simplest tonal control: one slider lifts or lowers overall brightness, the other expands or compresses contrast, both protecting highlight and shadow detail. The Use Legacy checkbox restores the crude pre-CS3 behaviour that clips aggressively.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Brightness/Contrast..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Brightness/Contrast.

parameters.name: Brightness
parameters.description: -150 to +150; shifts the whole tone curve.

parameters.name: Contrast
parameters.description: -50 to +100; steepens or flattens the curve around the midpoint.

parameters.name: Use Legacy
parameters.description: Reverts to the old linear, clipping algorithm.

tools.example: Add a Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer, Brightness +15, Contrast +20, then mask the sky out so only the foreground is affected.

tools.name: Levels
tools.description: Maps input black point, midtone (gamma) and white point onto an output range, per composite or per channel, with a live histogram. The standard first correction: drag the black and white input sliders to the ends of the histogram to set proper contrast, then move the grey slider for brightness. The three eyedroppers set black point, neutral grey and white point by clicking on the image.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Levels... (Ctrl+L), or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Levels.

parameters.name: Input Levels
parameters.description: Black point (0-253), gamma (9.99-0.10) and white point (2-255).

parameters.name: Output Levels
parameters.description: Compresses the result into a narrower range - used for faded/matte looks and for printing.

parameters.name: Channel
parameters.description: RGB composite or an individual channel, for removing colour casts.

parameters.name: Eyedroppers
parameters.description: Set black point, grey point (neutralises a cast) and white point by sampling the image.

parameters.name: Auto / Options
parameters.description: Enhance Monochromatic Contrast, Per Channel Contrast, Find Dark & Light Colors, Enhance Brightness and Contrast, with a clipping percentage.

tools.example:
1. Ctrl+L (or add a Levels adjustment layer).
2. Hold Alt and drag the black input slider until the first pixels appear - that is the clipping preview.
3. Repeat with the white slider, then set gamma to taste.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.adjustLevels(15, 240, 1.05, 0, 255);

tools.name: Curves
tools.description: The most powerful tonal and colour tool: an arbitrary input-to-output mapping edited by dragging points on a curve, per composite or per channel. An S-curve adds contrast, a lifted black point creates a matte film look, and channel curves correct or grade colour. The on-image adjustment (targeted) tool lets you drag directly on the photo to move the point that controls that tone.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Curves... (Ctrl+M), or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Curves.

parameters.name: Preset
parameters.description: Built-ins such as Strong Contrast, Negative, Cross Process, plus saved .acv files.

parameters.name: Channel
parameters.description: RGB composite or R, G, B (or C, M, Y, K) individually.

parameters.name: Targeted adjustment tool
parameters.description: Drag on the image to raise or lower the curve at that tonal value.

parameters.name: Show Clipping
parameters.description: Alt+drag an endpoint, or tick Show Clipping, to see blown highlights and blocked shadows.

parameters.name: Pencil / Smooth
parameters.description: Draw a freehand curve and smooth it - used for solarisation and posterised effects.

tools.example:
1. Add a Curves adjustment layer and set its blend mode to Luminosity.
2. Click a point at the 1/4 tone and pull it down, and one at the 3/4 tone and pull it up for a gentle S-curve.
3. Switch to the Blue channel and lift the shadows slightly for a cool-shadow grade.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.adjustCurves([[0,0],[64,48],[192,208],[255,255]]);

tools.name: Exposure
tools.description: Adjusts tone in a linear colour space, with Exposure affecting mainly the highlights, Offset the shadows and midtones, and Gamma Correction the midpoint. Designed for 32-bit HDR images but usable on 8- and 16-bit files for stops-based exposure changes.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Exposure..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Exposure.

parameters.name: Exposure
parameters.description: -20 to +20 stops; scales highlight values with minimal effect on black.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: -0.5 to +0.5; darkens or lightens shadows and midtones.

parameters.name: Gamma Correction
parameters.description: 9.99 to 0.01; a simple power-function midtone control.

tools.example: Add an Exposure adjustment layer, Exposure +0.35, Offset -0.01, Gamma 1.00, to lift an underexposed frame by roughly a third of a stop.

tools.name: Vibrance
tools.description: Raises the saturation of muted colours while protecting already saturated ones and skin tones, so it is far safer than Saturation for portraits and for general punch. The same dialog also carries a conventional Saturation slider.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Vibrance..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Vibrance.

parameters.name: Vibrance
parameters.description: -100 to +100; non-linear, protects skin tones and clipped colours.

parameters.name: Saturation
parameters.description: -100 to +100; linear saturation applied to every colour equally.

tools.example: Add a Vibrance adjustment layer, Vibrance +25, Saturation -5, for richer colour without orange skin.

tools.name: Hue/Saturation
tools.description: Shifts hue, saturation and lightness either globally (Master) or within one of six colour ranges whose boundaries can be dragged on the colour bar or set by sampling with the eyedroppers. Also the home of Colorize, which converts the image to a single tinted hue. The main tool for selective colour changes such as turning a red car blue.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Hue/Saturation... (Ctrl+U), or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Hue/Saturation.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Master, Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues, Magentas - or click the image with the targeted adjustment tool to pick the range automatically.

parameters.name: Hue
parameters.description: -180 to +180 degrees around the colour wheel.

parameters.name: Saturation / Lightness
parameters.description: -100 to +100 each.

parameters.name: Colorize
parameters.description: Maps the whole image to one hue, producing a monotone tint.

tools.example:
1. Add a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer.
2. Choose the targeted adjustment tool and drag left on the red car - Photoshop picks the Reds range.
3. Set Hue to -140 to turn it blue, then refine the range sliders so the skin tones are untouched.

tools.name: Color Balance
tools.description: Shifts the balance between complementary colour pairs (Cyan-Red, Magenta-Green, Yellow-Blue) separately in shadows, midtones and highlights. With Preserve Luminosity on it changes colour without altering brightness - a quick, intuitive grading tool for warming highlights and cooling shadows.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Color Balance... (Ctrl+B), or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Color Balance.

parameters.name: Tone
parameters.description: Shadows, Midtones or Highlights.

parameters.name: Cyan-Red / Magenta-Green / Yellow-Blue
parameters.description: -100 to +100 each.

parameters.name: Preserve Luminosity
parameters.description: Keeps overall brightness constant while colour changes.

tools.example: Add a Color Balance layer: Highlights +8 Red / +4 Yellow; Shadows +6 Blue. Preserve Luminosity on. Classic teal-and-orange grade.

tools.name: Black & White
tools.description: Converts to greyscale with per-colour control: six sliders decide how light or dark each original hue becomes, so a blue sky can be darkened dramatically while skin stays bright. The Tint option adds a duotone colour. Far better than Desaturate or Grayscale mode, which throw that control away.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Black & White... (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+B), or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Black & White.

parameters.name: Reds / Yellows / Greens / Cyans / Blues / Magentas
parameters.description: -200 to +300 each; the brightness each source hue maps to.

parameters.name: Preset
parameters.description: Red Filter, Infrared, High Contrast Blue Filter and other classic film emulations.

parameters.name: Tint / Hue / Saturation
parameters.description: Applies a single-colour tone such as sepia or selenium.

parameters.name: Targeted adjustment tool
parameters.description: Drag on an area of the photo to brighten or darken whichever hue dominates there.

tools.example:
1. Add a Black & White adjustment layer.
2. Drag down on the sky with the targeted adjustment tool - the Blues slider drops and the sky darkens.
3. Tick Tint, Hue 40 degrees, Saturation 12% for a warm split-tone.

tools.name: Photo Filter
tools.description: Simulates a coloured glass filter over the lens: warming (85, LBA, 81) and cooling (80, LBB, 82) filters plus named colours, or any custom colour, applied at an adjustable density. With Preserve Luminosity on the image keeps its brightness.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Photo Filter..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Photo Filter.

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: Preset warming/cooling filters and named colours (Sepia, Deep Blue, Underwater, ...).

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Any custom colour instead of a preset.

parameters.name: Density
parameters.description: 1-100% strength of the filter.

parameters.name: Preserve Luminosity
parameters.description: Prevents the filter from darkening the image.

tools.example: Add a Photo Filter layer, Warming Filter (85), Density 20%, Preserve Luminosity on, to warm an overcast shot.

tools.name: Channel Mixer
tools.description: Builds each output channel from a weighted mixture of the source channels, with a Constant offset. Used for high-quality black-and-white conversions (tick Monochrome), for swapping or repairing damaged channels, and for infrared-style colour effects.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Channel Mixer..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Channel Mixer.

parameters.name: Output Channel
parameters.description: Which channel the mix is written to (Red, Green, Blue, or Gray when Monochrome is on).

parameters.name: Source Channels
parameters.description: -200% to +200% each; keeping the total near 100% preserves overall brightness.

parameters.name: Constant
parameters.description: -200% to +200% brightness offset added to the output channel.

parameters.name: Monochrome
parameters.description: Produces a greyscale result from a custom channel mix.

tools.example: Add a Channel Mixer layer, tick Monochrome, set Red 40%, Green 40%, Blue 20% for a natural black-and-white conversion of a portrait.

tools.name: Color Lookup
tools.description: Applies a 3D colour lookup table (LUT) - the same .cube, .3dl, .look or .icc profiles used in video grading - as a single-click grade. Photoshop ships a set of presets, and Abstract/Device Link profiles and external LUTs can be loaded. File > Export > Color Lookup Tables exports the current adjustment stack as a LUT for use elsewhere.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Color Lookup..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Color Lookup.

parameters.name: 3DLUT File
parameters.description: Built-in presets (Crisp Warm, Fuji F125 Kodak 2395, TealOrangePlusContrast, ...) or Load 3D LUT for a .cube/.3dl file.

parameters.name: Abstract / Device Link
parameters.description: ICC-profile-based alternatives to a 3D LUT.

parameters.name: Dither
parameters.description: Reduces banding in the mapped result.

tools.example:
1. Add a Color Lookup adjustment layer.
2. Choose 3DLUT File > Load 3D LUT... and pick your house grade .cube.
3. Drop its opacity to 60% to dial back the effect.

tools.name: Invert
tools.description: Inverts every channel value (255 minus the value), turning a positive into a negative. Used for converting scanned film negatives (usually with per-channel Levels afterwards to remove the orange mask), for flipping a mask, and inside frequency-separation and high-pass workflows.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Invert (Ctrl+I), or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Invert.
tools.example:
Select a layer mask and press Ctrl+I to swap what is hidden and shown.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.invert();

tools.name: Posterize
tools.description: Reduces each channel to a specified number of tonal levels, producing flat bands of colour. Used for poster and screen-print looks, for visualising tonal transitions and banding, and for generating simplified masks.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Posterize..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Posterize.

parameters.name: Levels
parameters.description: 2-255 tonal levels per channel; 4-8 gives the classic poster effect.

tools.example: Add a Posterize adjustment layer with Levels = 5, then add a Black & White layer beneath it for a screen-print style graphic.

tools.name: Threshold
tools.description: Converts the image to pure black and white at a chosen luminance cut-off. Its main production use is diagnostic: add a temporary Threshold layer and slide to the extremes to find the darkest and lightest pixels for placing Levels/Curves black and white points, or Color Sampler points.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Threshold..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Threshold.

parameters.name: Threshold Level
parameters.description: 1-255 luminance cut-off; below becomes black, above becomes white.

tools.example:
1. Add a Threshold layer and drag the slider left until only a few white spots remain - that is the brightest point.
2. Mark it with the Color Sampler tool (Shift+I).
3. Delete the Threshold layer and set the white point in Curves on that sample.

tools.name: Gradient Map
tools.description: Maps the image's tonal range onto a gradient: shadows take the left colour, highlights the right. Used for split-toning, duotones, colour grading and instant stylised looks; at low opacity or in Soft Light mode it is one of the cleanest grading methods available.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Gradient Map..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Gradient Map.

parameters.name: Gradient
parameters.description: Any gradient preset; click it to edit the stops and their midpoints.

parameters.name: Dither
parameters.description: Adds noise to prevent banding.

parameters.name: Reverse
parameters.description: Swaps the shadow and highlight ends.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Perceptual, Linear or Classic gradient interpolation (Photoshop 2022 and later).

tools.example:
1. Add a Gradient Map layer with a deep blue to warm cream gradient.
2. Set the layer to Soft Light at 40%.
3. Paint black on its mask over the skin to keep skin tones neutral.

tools.name: Selective Color
tools.description: Adjusts the amount of cyan, magenta, yellow and black in each of nine colour families (reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks). A print-oriented tool that is also the finest control available for subtle grading - adding a little cyan to the Blacks cools shadows without touching anything else.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Selective Color..., or Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Selective Color.

parameters.name: Colors
parameters.description: Which colour family is being edited.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Relative (proportional to existing ink) or Absolute (fixed percentage change).

tools.example: Add a Selective Color layer: Colors = Neutrals, Cyan +3, Yellow -4, Black +2. Then Colors = Blacks, Cyan +5 for cool shadows.

tools.name: Shadows/Highlights
tools.description: Recovers detail in blocked shadows and blown highlights by applying a local, radius-based tonal correction rather than a global curve. Show More Options exposes Tonal Width, Radius, Color and Midtone controls that prevent the flat, haloed look the default settings can produce.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Shadows/Highlights... (no adjustment-layer version - apply it to a smart object so it becomes a re-editable smart filter).

parameters.name: Shadows: Amount / Tone / Radius
parameters.description: How much lifting, over what tonal range, and the size of the local neighbourhood.

parameters.name: Highlights: Amount / Tone / Radius
parameters.description: The same three controls for pulling highlights down.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Saturation compensation for the corrected areas.

parameters.name: Midtone
parameters.description: Contrast adjustment for the midtones after the correction.

tools.example:
1. Convert the layer to a smart object.
2. Image > Adjustments > Shadows/Highlights, tick Show More Options.
3. Shadows Amount 25%, Tone 40%, Radius 60 px; Highlights Amount 12%, Radius 60 px.
tools.notes: Large Radius values give a natural result; very small ones cause halos around high-contrast edges. See also the Camera Raw Filter entry in the Filters category.

tools.name: HDR Toning
tools.description: Applies high-dynamic-range tone mapping to a single flattened image, with Local Adaptation, Exposure and Gamma, Highlight Compression and Equalize Histogram methods plus edge glow, detail and a tone curve. It requires a flattened document and is therefore usually the final step of an HDR merge or a deliberately gritty, detailed look.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > HDR Toning... (flattens the document).

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Local Adaptation, Equalize Histogram, Exposure and Gamma, Highlight Compression.

parameters.name: Edge Glow: Radius / Strength
parameters.description: Size and intensity of the local contrast halo.

parameters.name: Tone and Detail
parameters.description: Gamma, Exposure, Detail, Shadow and Highlight.

parameters.name: Advanced: Vibrance / Saturation
parameters.description: Colour strength of the tone-mapped result.

tools.example:
1. Merge the bracketed exposures with File > Automate > Merge to HDR Pro (32-bit) and save.
2. Image > Adjustments > HDR Toning, Method = Local Adaptation, Radius 60 px, Strength 0.6, Detail +25%.
tools.notes: Photoshop warns that the document will be flattened - duplicate the file first.

tools.name: Match Color
tools.description: Transfers the colour statistics of one image (or one layer, or a selection) onto another so that separately shot frames match, and can also neutralise a cast within a single image. Luminance, Color Intensity and Fade control the strength, and Neutralize removes a colour cast automatically.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Match Color... (RGB mode only).

parameters.name: Source / Layer
parameters.description: Which open document and layer supplies the target colour statistics.

parameters.name: Luminance / Color Intensity
parameters.description: Brightness and saturation of the matched result.

parameters.name: Fade
parameters.description: Blends back towards the original.

parameters.name: Neutralize
parameters.description: Removes a colour cast from the destination image.

parameters.name: Use Selection in Source/Target
parameters.description: Restricts the statistics to a selected region.

tools.example:
1. Open the reference shot and the shot to correct.
2. With the second active, Image > Adjustments > Match Color.
3. Set Source to the reference document, tick Neutralize, and set Fade to 30% if the match is too strong.

tools.name: Replace Color
tools.description: Combines a Color Range selection with a Hue/Saturation adjustment in one dialog: sample the colour to change with the eyedroppers, widen or narrow the match with Fuzziness, then shift its hue, saturation and lightness. Fast for recolouring a product in a batch of shots.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Replace Color...

parameters.name: Eyedroppers
parameters.description: Sample, add to and subtract from the colour being matched.

parameters.name: Fuzziness
parameters.description: 0-200; how far from the sampled colour the mask extends.

parameters.name: Localized Color Clusters
parameters.description: Keeps the match spatially coherent, avoiding stray pixels elsewhere.

parameters.name: Hue / Saturation / Lightness
parameters.description: The replacement colour shift, or click Result to pick it directly.

tools.example:
1. Image > Adjustments > Replace Color.
2. Click the green bottle, Shift+click the shadowed side to extend the match, Fuzziness 45.
3. Drag Hue to -90 to turn it purple.

tools.name: Equalize
tools.description: Redistributes pixel values so the histogram spans the full range as evenly as possible, mapping the darkest pixel to black and the lightest to white. A blunt instrument for photographs, but useful for revealing faint detail in scientific, scanned or very flat images.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Equalize. With an active selection Photoshop asks whether to equalize the selection only or the whole image based on it.
tools.example:
1. Select a faint region of a scanned document.
2. Image > Adjustments > Equalize, choose "Equalize entire image based on selected area".

tools.name: Desaturate
tools.description: Strips all saturation from the layer or selection, leaving a greyscale result in the current colour mode. Fast but crude - there is no control over how each hue maps to grey, so the Black & White adjustment is almost always the better choice.
tools.usage: Image > Adjustments > Desaturate (Shift+Ctrl+U).
tools.example:
Ctrl+J to duplicate the layer, Shift+Ctrl+U to desaturate it, then mask it back selectively.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.desaturate();

tools.name: Auto Tone
tools.description: Sets the black and white points of each channel independently, which fixes both contrast and most colour casts in one keystroke. A reasonable starting point on flat scans and snapshots; its behaviour is controlled by the algorithm and clipping settings in the Levels/Curves Auto Options dialog.
tools.usage: Image > Auto Tone (Shift+Ctrl+L).
tools.example:
Shift+Ctrl+L on a flat scan, then refine with a Curves layer.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.autoLevels();
tools.notes: Destructive. For a non-destructive equivalent, add a Levels layer and Alt+click Auto to choose the algorithm.

tools.name: Auto Contrast
tools.description: Sets black and white points from the composite image rather than per channel, so it improves contrast without shifting colour balance. Use it when Auto Tone introduces an unwanted colour change.
tools.usage: Image > Auto Contrast (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+L).
tools.example:
Alt+Shift+Ctrl+L on a hazy landscape to restore contrast while keeping the existing colour balance.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.autoContrast();

tools.name: Auto Color
tools.description: Neutralises midtones and clips highlights and shadows using the Find Dark & Light Colors algorithm with Snap Neutral Midtones enabled, correcting both contrast and colour cast. Often the best of the three Auto commands on everyday photographs.
tools.usage: Image > Auto Color (Shift+Ctrl+B).
tools.example: Shift+Ctrl+B on a photo with a green cast from fluorescent lighting; follow with a Photo Filter layer if it overcorrects.

tools.name: Camera Raw Filter (as an adjustment)
tools.description: Brings the whole Camera Raw editing environment - Basic panel (Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vibrance, Saturation), Curve, Color Mixer, Color Grading, Optics, Geometry, Effects, Detail and local masking with Select Subject/Sky/Objects - to bear on any layer inside Photoshop. Applied to a smart object it becomes a fully re-editable smart filter, which makes it the single most capable adjustment in the application.
tools.usage: Filter > Camera Raw Filter... (Shift+Ctrl+A). Convert the layer to a smart object first so the settings stay editable.

parameters.name: Basic
parameters.description: Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vibrance, Saturation, white balance.

parameters.name: Masking
parameters.description: Subject, Sky, Background, Objects, People, Brush, Linear and Radial gradients, Colour and Luminance ranges, all with the full slider set.

parameters.name: Color Grading
parameters.description: Three-way colour wheels for shadows, midtones and highlights with blending and balance.

parameters.name: Optics / Geometry
parameters.description: Profile-based lens corrections, defringing and Upright perspective correction.

tools.example:
1. Right-click the layer > Convert to Smart Object.
2. Shift+Ctrl+A to open Camera Raw Filter.
3. Basic: Highlights -40, Shadows +30, Texture +10, Dehaze +8; then add a Sky mask and drop its exposure by 0.5 stops.
4. OK - the settings remain editable by double-clicking the smart filter.
